analysis.title: SoFi Technologies Inc. (SOFI): 3Q26 First Take: Beat and raise and better than expected 2027 guidance
key_insights: SOFI reported a 3Q26 beat and raise on revenue and EPS. The beat came mainly from higher loan origination activity, which lifted both net interest income and fair value origination gains in fee income.
Originations of $16.9bn were 17% above consensus ($14.4bn) and 14% above GS's estimate, driven mainly by personal loans (Personal $12.6bn vs consensus $10.1bn).
Adjusted revenue was $1,371mn, about 8% above consensus ($1,264mn). Net interest income was $929.5mn, 9% above consensus ($853mn), on interest income of $1,343mn and interest expense of $414mn.
Net interest margin was 6.14% vs consensus 5.91% and 5.98% in 2Q26, helped by higher balances and better yield dynamics.
Non-interest income was $456mn, 8% above consensus ($419mn per Exhibit 1). Loan origination, sales and securitization income was $152mn vs consensus $107mn.
Adjusted EBITDA was $470mn, 6% above consensus ($443mn), with a 34.3% margin. GAAP net income was $241mn and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.18 vs consensus $0.17.

FY26 guidance was raised: adjusted net revenue ~$5.04bn (from ~$4.75-4.85bn), adjusted EBITDA ~$1.66bn (from ~$1.6bn), adjusted net income ~$840mn (from $825mn), adjusted diluted EPS ~$0.61 (from ~$0.60).
Initial FY27 guidance: adjusted net revenue ~$6.4bn, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.24bn, adjusted net income ~$1.28bn, adjusted diluted EPS ~$0.90, about 10% above consensus EPS of $0.82 (Visible Alpha).
Marks as a percentage of loans fell sequentially. GS says this was offset by stronger originations and likely a benefit from interest rate hedging.
CET1 capital fell to 16.9% from 18.7% in 2Q26 (a 182bps decline) and 20.0% in 3Q25. GS flags capital levels as a call question.
GS believes sentiment was negative going into the print and that SOFI faces no significant revenue or capital headwinds from higher rates, so it expects the stock to trade well on the print.
GS rates SOFI Neutral with a $15 12-month price target (19x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates), implying 3.7% upside from $14.46.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $15 target (19x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates) despite the beat and raise. It expects the stock to trade well on the print, with 3.7% upside to target from the $14.46 close on 26 Oct 2026.

earnings_insights: SOFI 3Q26 reported 10/27: adjusted revenue $1,371mn vs consensus $1,264mn (Visible Alpha) and GS est. $1,284mn. Total revenue was $1,385mn before adjustments.
SOFI 3Q26 reported GAAP diluted EPS $0.18 vs consensus $0.17 and GS est. $0.15. Net income was $241mn vs consensus $227mn.
SOFI 3Q26 reported adjusted EBITDA $470mn vs consensus $443mn and GS est. $423mn.
SOFI 3Q26 net interest income was $929mn vs consensus $853mn and GS est. $870mn. NIM was 6.14% vs consensus 5.91%.
SOFI 3Q26 total loan originations were $16.9bn vs consensus $14.4bn: Personal $12.6bn (including $3.8bn Loan Platform Business), Student $2.9bn, Home $1.4bn.

SOFI FY26 guidance (company, given 10/27): adjusted net revenue ~$5.04bn vs consensus $4,882mn, adjusted EBITDA ~$1.66bn vs consensus $1,628mn, adjusted EPS ~$0.61 vs consensus $0.59. Implied 4Q26 adjusted EPS is $0.19, in line with consensus $0.19.

SOFI FY27 guidance (company, initial): adjusted net revenue ~$6.4bn vs consensus $6,054mn, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.24bn vs consensus $2,115mn, net income ~$1.28bn vs consensus $1,141mn, adjusted EPS ~$0.90 vs consensus $0.82.
Selling and marketing expense was $444mn vs consensus $360mn (up 55% y/y). G&A was $201mn vs consensus $209mn.

macro_indicators.reading: Higher rates are not a significant headwind to SOFI revenue or capital
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS says SOFI faces no significant revenue or capital headwinds from higher rates, and that a likely interest rate hedging benefit helped marks.

vol_and_positioning: GS believes sentiment was negative heading into the print, which supports a positive stock reaction to the beat and raise.
